HOME.TITLE: Home
HOME.HERO_SUBTITLE: Drop bombs, blow up crates, grab power-ups and be the last one standing. The classic arena battle, online and in the browser.
HOME.PODIUM_LEAD: The top three of the online ranking, as the character they last played. Wins count; luck too.
HOME.PODIUM_EMPTY: The podium is empty. The first online win goes up here.
HOME.MODE_LOCAL_TITLE_VIDEO: Offline: Faísca breaks a crate, picks up the fire it hid and catches Dra. Lia with a bigger blast.
HOME.MODE_ONLINE_TITLE_VIDEO: Online: five in the arena and the next in line on the wall; a bomb thrown in catches Tião and the thrower takes his place.
HOME.MODE_LOCAL_DESC: Against the bots, or two players on the same keyboard. Best of friends, until the first bomb.
HOME.MODE_ONLINE_DESC: One public arena for up to 5 players over the internet. Join the queue and, while you wait, throw bombs in from outside the wall: a kill puts you in.
HOME.HOW_SUBTITLE: Four rules — that is the whole game.
HOME.HOW_1_DESC: A bomb explodes in a cross after a few seconds. You can walk off your own bomb, but not back onto it.
HOME.HOW_2_DESC: Crates break; stone blocks never do. Flames stop at the first crate they hit.
HOME.HOW_3_DESC: Destroyed blocks may hide upgrades. Careful: a flame destroys an exposed power-up too.
HOME.HOW_4_DESC: Bombs set each other off in chain reactions. If the last two fall together, it is a draw.
HOME.POWERUPS_SUBTITLE: They hide under the crates. Pick them up before the fire does.
HOME.POWERUP_BOMB_DESC: One more bomb on the field at a time.
HOME.CONTROLS_SUBTITLE: Two players on one keyboard, or the on-screen controller on a phone.
HOME.CONTROLS_PHONE_HINT: Go full screen on a phone and the controller appears over the arena. To move, touch anywhere on the left half: the pad comes to your thumb and follows it.
HOME.CTA_FINAL_SUBTITLE: Join the arena and light the fuse.
HOME.FACT_1: Up to 5 online, bots to practise
HOME.PREVIEW_ALT: A match in the arena: four players, a bomb about to go off and a blast breaking crates.
HOME.POWERUP_PIERCE_DESC: The flame goes through crates and burns every one in its path.
HOME.POWERUP_REMOTE_DESC: Your bombs wait: the detonate button (E or /) sets off the oldest.
HOME.POWERUP_VEST_DESC: Eight seconds in which fire cannot reach you.
HOME.POWERUP_GLOVE_DESC: Pick up a bomb and throw it three tiles ahead, over anything.
HOME.POWERUP_KICK_DESC: Walk into a bomb and it hops a tile away.
HOME.PRESENCE_NONE: Nobody online right now — be the first
HOME.LIVE_LEAD: Not a video: the real game, played by bots under the same rules, on the usual map.
HOME.MODES_LEAD: Online against whoever is around, offline with a friend beside you, or as a group against the city's creatures.
HOME.MODE_ONLINE_META: Up to 5 players · over the internet
HOME.MODE_CAMPAIGN_DESC: Creatures have taken over the city. Cross every area with up to 3 friends, stage by stage, all the way to the boss.
HOME.MODE_CAMPAIGN_TITLE_VIDEO: Campaign: leafcutter ants, pigeons and a snail march across the lawn at the Novato and Faísca, and the queen ant waits at the end.
HOME.HOW_BOARD_ALT: A slice of the arena acts the rules out: a player drops a bomb and steps away, the cross of fire breaks a crate and stops at the pillars, they grab the power-up it hid, and one bomb sets off another and knocks the rival out.

CHARACTERS.TITLE: Characters
CHARACTERS.LEAD: Meet the crew. Pick who you play as, turn them around, see them walk, and mount up.

NOVATO.NAME: Rookie
NOVATO.STORY: The Rookie read the rules once, in the queue, and decided that was plenty. No job, no uniform, no gear: a cap, a tee and a confidence nobody can explain. Drops the first bomb and stays to watch what happens. Everyone started like this; the others just do not admit it.

FAISCA.NAME: Faísca
FAISCA.STORY: Faísca defused bombs in the army until he noticed arming them was more fun. He reaches the arena before everyone else, purely out of the habit of waking at five. Tired Dev and Dr. Lia call him "the only adult in the group", and he pretends not to hear.

BYTE.NAME: Tired Dev
BYTE.STORY: Tired Dev has been awake for 36 hours over a bug that turned out to be a semicolon. He joined the arena because "it's like a production deploy, just with fewer explosions". Dr. Lia has told him to sleep three times; he answered "one more coffee".

GESTORA.NAME: Stressed Manager
GESTORA.STORY: The Manager does not suffer through meetings: she books every one of them. Daily at 9, alignment at 10, "pre-alignment for the alignment" at 11 and a surprise one-on-one with Tired Dev right after lunch. If anyone's calendar shows fifteen free minutes, the invite has already landed. She is the one who woke Tired Dev at 3 a.m. over the semicolon bug, and the one who promised the client "it ships by Friday". She joined the arena to "unblock the team" and found that a bomb unblocks things far faster than a Jira ticket. She does not sleep either: after 6 p.m. she finally opens the editor to write her own code.

CEO.NAME: Jittery CEO
CEO.STORY: The CEO has not slept since the funding round. At 2:50 a.m. he is still refreshing the cash chart on his phone, and it only goes down; at 2:55 he calls the Manager, which is why at 3 she wakes Tired Dev. He is the one who sold the client an "AI-powered" feature that does not exist yet, and now he meets the investors on Monday. He is on his fourth energy drink, his right eye twitches on its own and he smiles with his teeth clenched: "it's all great, team, it's all great". He joined the arena because he read that blowing things up is "disruption". When a bomb goes wrong it is not a failure: it is a pivot.

TESTER.NAME: Contrarian Tester
TESTER.STORY: The Contrarian Tester says "no" before he has finished reading the ticket. He reopened the semicolon bug three times, "just to be safe", and swears the two-and-a-half-second fuse is out of spec: "the document said three". When Tired Dev says "it works on my machine", he answers "then ship your machine to the client". He disagrees with the Manager at the daily, with the CEO at the all-hands and with the scoreboard at the end of the match. He carries a magnifying glass and a REJECTED stamp; the glass is only there to look as if he read it.

INFRA.NAME: The Infra Guy
INFRA.STORY: The staging environment has been down since March, and the ticket is with the Infra Guy, "in progress". He has the key to every room, the password to every server and no hurry at all: "I'll look at it Monday". When Tired Dev's deploy hangs it is DNS; when it is not DNS it is the cache; when it is not the cache he has already gone to heat the water for his chimarrão. The CEO asks every day when the new server goes up, and the answer is always "it's provisioning". In the arena he is the only one who never runs: he says a two-and-a-half-second fuse is "just latency".

STAFF.NAME: On-Call Staff
STAFF.STORY: The Staff engineer has been at the company for fifteen years and is the only one who knows why that "if" from 2011 exists, the one nobody dares delete. He lives putting out fires: the CEO sells what does not exist, the Manager promises Friday, the Dev deploys on Friday at 6 p.m., the Tester rejects everything and the Infra Guy "will look on Monday", and the on-call pager goes off in his pocket. He never says no; he says "leave it with me", grabs the extinguisher and goes. He joined the arena because, for him, explosions are routine: "I've seen worse deploys". When someone drops a bomb, he gets there before the fire does.

LIA.NAME: Dr. Lia
LIA.STORY: Dr. Lia plays the way she does rounds: walks in, reads the whole arena in two seconds and already knows who is not leaving. She times the fuse by pulse, two and a half seconds, no watch needed. She triages opponents: green, yellow, red, and whoever gets a bomb next to them becomes a "former patient". She finds the opponent behind the crate the way she finds a hard vein: in the dark, first try, no apology.

MOTOCA.NAME: Zé Motoca
MOTOCA.STORY: Zé Motoca joined the arena because the app put a delivery there, and he never cancels a ride. He already knows every shortcut between the crates, because shortcuts are the specialty. He says a bomb with a two-and-a-half-second fuse is "plenty of time, the customer hasn't even come downstairs". The only one on foot by choice: "the bag doesn't fit on the back seat".

TIAO.NAME: Tião
TIAO.STORY: Tião has looked after the Substation for twenty-two years and has never had a shock, or at least never mentioned one. He joined the arena because someone tripped the neighbourhood breaker, and he is not leaving until it is back on. He taps every crate with his screwdriver before getting close, calls the transformers by name and swears the blackout every minute is "the power company's fault". The moustache predates college; the hard hat predates the moustache.

CHARACTERS.SEE_MOUNTS: See the mounts and their abilities →

MOUNTS.TITLE: Mounts
MOUNTS.LEAD: A mount belongs to nobody. Blow up a crate, find an egg, pick it up, and it hatches into one of these at random. Riding, you move faster, the mount takes the first hit for you, and each one has an ability: Shift for player 1, Ctrl for player 2.

TATU.NAME: Tatu
TATU.STORY: Tatu was the mascot of Faísca's barracks and followed him out. Faísca swears he is fast; nobody believed him until the arena, where for a second and a half everyone sees it.
TATU.ABILITY_DESC: Rolls straight ahead at nearly double speed and can't turn until it stops: against a wall, crate or bomb, on a second press, or after crossing the arena. Still drops bombs, still takes hits. No cooldown.

PATO.NAME: Pato
PATO.STORY: Pato started as a bath toy on Tired Dev's desk, listening to bug explanations at three in the morning. From all that listening, he grew. He is the only one on the team who understands Tired Dev's code, and he tells no one.
PATO.ABILITY_DESC: Hops over the next cell — crate, pillar or bomb — and lands on the one after; if that one is taken, no jump. Never over the arena's edge. Nothing touches you in the air. No cooldown.

BERNARDO.NAME: Bernardo
BERNARDO.STORY: Bernardo was trained to rescue climbers but has never seen a mountain. In his cask he carries Dr. Lia's medicine and, in secret, biscuits. He wags his tail at opponents too, which Dr. Lia files under "ethical concerns".
BERNARDO.ABILITY_DESC: Drops 3 bombs at once: one under you and one on each free cell ahead, over your bomb limit. The line stops at the first crate or bomb. No cooldown.

CAPIVARA.NAME: Capivara
CAPIVARA.STORY: The Capivara did not choose the arena; the arena was built around her and she saw no reason to leave. She runs at 35 km/h when she wants to, and she never wants to. She is the only mount opponents stop to greet. The bird is staff, not decoration: it warns when the fuse is about to run out.
CAPIVARA.ABILITY_DESC: Walks over bombs, yours and anyone's. No button, no cooldown.

GALINHA.NAME: Galinha
GALINHA.STORY: Galinha lived on the roof of the Substation and spent years pecking at the wires before anyone noticed she had been charging herself. She lays no eggs; she trips breakers. Tião fitted her with a saddle after she rebooted the whole arena with one sneeze. Nobody strokes her twice.
GALINHA.ABILITY_DESC: A jolt that sets off every bomb within 2 cells, yours and anyone's, at once. No cooldown.

ARENAS.TITLE: Arenas
ARENAS.LIVE: The previews are live matches, played by the game's rules on each arena.
ARENAS.LEAD: Where a round is played. Same 15 × 13 grid and the same rules everywhere; each arena is a place with its own look and one special moment. Pick one and play, or share its link.
ARENAS.SOON_DESC: A new arena is on the drawing board. It lands in a coming update.
ARENAS.LINK_HINT: Add &seed=1234 so everyone gets the same crates.
ARENAS.PIECES_LEAD: Every tile the arena is built from, at the arena’s size and zoomed.

SUBESTACAO.NAME: Substation
SUBESTACAO.DESC: Transformer cabinets for pillars, fuse boxes for crates, cracked concrete with a safety stripe, a fenced barrier around the edge and the generator humming in the middle.
SUBESTACAO.MOMENT_DESC: Every 30 s the lights go out for 2 s: only bombs, flames and silhouettes are left.
SUBESTACAO.NOTE_1: A steel cabinet with cooling fins, a warning sign and a red LED out of step with its neighbours. Indestructible; a flame that touches it sparks, visually only.
SUBESTACAO.NOTE_2_TITLE: The middle is the fifth spawn
SUBESTACAO.NOTE_2: The generator moved out of the centre cell: with five players, the middle corner-less spot is a spawn like the four corners, with the same free box around it.
SUBESTACAO.NOTE_3: Yellow, with the high-voltage bolt. They break like crates and may hide a power-up; the splinters are sparks.

AUTODROMO.NAME: Race track
AUTODROMO.DESC: Asphalt with skid marks, stacks of painted tyres for pillars, fuel drums for crates, a guard-rail on a red-and-white kerb, the grandstand along the top and the start lights in the middle.
AUTODROMO.MOMENT_DESC: It rains on the track all race long: drops streak the screen and the asphalt shines.
AUTODROMO.NOTE_1: Three tyres, the top one painted in red and white like a corner barrier. Indestructible; a flame that touches it makes the top tyre bounce, visually only.
AUTODROMO.NOTE_2_TITLE: The middle is the fifth spawn
AUTODROMO.NOTE_2: The start lights left the centre cell: with five players it is a spawn like the four corners, with the same free box around it.
AUTODROMO.NOTE_3: Red, with steel rims and the flammable diamond. They break like crates; the splinters are a short burst of flame.

GRAMADO.NAME: Gramado
GRAMADO.DESC: A mown lawn in a walled yard: cut stone cubes for pillars, clay-brick blocks for crates, a dry-stone wall with a hedge along the top, and an old well. The plain arena — the one to learn on, and the quick versus.
GRAMADO.MOMENT_DESC: No blackout, no rain: full light and a dry lawn the whole round. What you see is what you get.
GRAMADO.NOTE_1: Cut stone with chisel marks and moss at the foot. Indestructible, and nothing in them to surprise you.
GRAMADO.NOTE_2_TITLE: The centre is the fifth spawn
GRAMADO.NOTE_2: The well stays out of the grid: with five players, the middle is a spawn like the four corners, with the same clear space around it.
GRAMADO.NOTE_3: Clay bricks and mortar, moss in one corner. They break like crates and may hide a power-up.

NUCLEO.NAME: Núcleo
NUCLEO.DESC: The datacenter where CIDA, the AI that runs the city, lives: a circuit-board floor, server racks for pillars, glass data cubes for crates, a barrier with a light strip around the edge and a wall of screens along the top, her eye in the middle.
NUCLEO.MOMENT_DESC: Every 30 s the eye turns red and a laser line runs down the arena in 2 s. It only looks: it burns nobody.
NUCLEO.NOTE_1: Servers with bays, vents and blinking LEDs. Indestructible.
NUCLEO.NOTE_2_TITLE: The eye is on the top wall
NUCLEO.NOTE_2: CIDA’s eye is a screen in the top wall, not a cell of the board: the centre is still the fifth spawn.
NUCLEO.NOTE_3: Glass with a lit core in a light frame, so they read as breakable. They break like crates and may hide a power-up.

PROGRAMADOR.NAME: Coder’s Arena
PROGRAMADOR.DESC: The company’s open-plan office, where the Dev, the Manager, the CEO, the Tester, the Infra Guy and the Staff work: office carpet, desks with monitors for pillars, stacks of pizza boxes for crates, cubicle partitions around the edge and whiteboards along the top, with the CI screen in the middle. From the kitchen window, the Pizza Bot throws pizzas into the arena.
PROGRAMADOR.MOMENT_DESC: Every 30 s the CI screen says FAILED, the siren lights up and every monitor turns red for 2 s. Only a look: it changes nothing in play.
PROGRAMADOR.NOTE_1: Every 20 s he juggles, marks a cell with a red target and throws a pizza. On a bomb: the bomb goes out and a stack of boxes stands there, maybe with an item. On the floor: a stack of boxes too. On someone’s head: cheese in the face, slow for 2 s.
PROGRAMADOR.NOTE_2: A monitor full of code and, beside it, a mug, an energy drink or a rubber duck. Indestructible.
PROGRAMADOR.NOTE_3: Three delivery boxes stacked up, the order slip taped on. They break like crates and can hide a power-up.

ITEMS.TITLE: Items
ITEMS.LEAD: What hides under the crates. Some raise a number, others change your bomb or the way you walk, one protects you, the egg hatches a mount — and the skull gets in your way. The ones marked for stages show up in the campaign.
ITEMS.SIZES: Side by side, at the arena’s size
ITEMS.SIZES_LEAD: The first tile is what the player sees. The rest is zoom.
ITEMS.STAGES_LEAD: The crack grows as a player comes within a tile; on pick-up the shell opens and the mount appears.

EGG.NAME: Egg
EGG.DESC: Big, on the floor with its shadow, lit by the arena’s cool rim light, with teal patches of its own. It wobbles; near a player it cracks.
EGG.EFFECT: Hatches a random mount for whoever picks it up.
EGG.NOTE_1: Bomb, fire and skates are numbers, and the glass panel says “bonus”. The egg is a creature about to be born: it sits on the floor with a shadow, so it stands out without shouting.
EGG.NOTE_2: Teal, the arena’s accent, in soft rounded shapes. Nothing that reads as somebody else’s egg.
EGG.NOTE_3: Idle, it rocks a few degrees. Within a tile of a player it cracks stage by stage: it says “alive” without a word, and everybody runs for it.

BOMB.NAME: Extra bomb
BOMB.DESC: A glass tile with a small bomb and a lit fuse.
BOMB.EFFECT: One more bomb on the field at a time.
BOMB.NOTE_1: The same blue as the HUD’s bomb counter, so the pickup and the number read as one thing.
BOMB.NOTE_2: Numbers come on glass tiles; living things do not. The contrast is what makes the egg special.
BOMB.NOTE_3: Past eight bombs the field is already full; more would only slow the round.

FIRE.NAME: Fire
FIRE.DESC: A glass tile with a flame.
FIRE.NOTE_1: The flame’s own gradient, from yellow to red, is the one the blast uses.
FIRE.NOTE_2: Range decides fights; eight are hidden per arena, as many as bombs.
FIRE.NOTE_3: Eight tiles of fire cross most of the arena; more would make corners unsafe.

SPEED.NAME: Skates
SPEED.DESC: A glass tile with a lightning bolt.
SPEED.NOTE_1: Speed in the modern idiom: one shape that reads at 64 px.
SPEED.NOTE_2: Speed is the rarest: too much of it and the corridors stop feeling tight.
SPEED.NOTE_3: A mount gives its own bonus on top; the two stack, up to the cap.

PIERCE.NAME: Piercing bomb
PIERCE.EFFECT: The flame of your bombs goes through crates and burns every one in its path.
PIERCE.DESC: A red glass tile with a bolt going through a crate.
PIERCE.NOTE_1: The same colour a piercing bomb gets in the arena, so the item and the bomb read as one thing.
PIERCE.NOTE_2: Once picked up, every bomb of yours pierces until the round ends. Hence one per arena.
PIERCE.NOTE_3: It goes through crates, bombs and exposed power-ups; stone still stops everything.

REMOTE.NAME: Remote control
REMOTE.EFFECT: Your bombs have no fuse. The detonate button (E for player 1, / for player 2) sets off the oldest, whenever you want.
REMOTE.DESC: A blue glass tile with a remote: antenna and red button.
REMOTE.NOTE_1: Detonating has a key of its own: E for player 1, / for player 2. The bomb button still only drops bombs, never detonates, so you set them off when you choose, however many are down.
REMOTE.NOTE_2: A remote bomb sits blue-tinted on the floor. Whoever sees it knows it will not go off by itself.
REMOTE.NOTE_3: A flame touching a remote bomb sets it off at once, like any other. Traps carry risk.

VEST.NAME: Vest
VEST.EFFECT: For eight seconds fire cannot reach you.
VEST.DESC: A teal glass tile with a shield.
VEST.NOTE_1: The character alternates white and teal until it runs out, and the HUD counts the seconds. Nobody is caught off guard.
VEST.NOTE_2_TITLE: Protects the rider, not the mount
VEST.NOTE_2: With the vest, the flame passes you entirely, mount included. Without it, the mount takes the hit first.
VEST.NOTE_3: Eight immune seconds decide a fight. More than one and the round becomes a race for vests.

ITEMS.SOUNDS_LEAD: What plays when this item is picked up, and what the announcer may say. Press to hear.
ITEMS.KEYS_HINT: The bomb key keeps dropping bombs; this one sets off the oldest remote bomb, whenever you choose.

GLOVE.NAME: Glove
GLOVE.EFFECT: Drop a bomb and, before stepping off it, press the bomb key again to pick it up; press once more to throw it three tiles ahead. Facing a player right next to you, the bomb key lifts them instead: they ride overhead for up to two seconds, and the bomb key throws them three tiles, landing dizzy for a second. Bombs and players fly over anything and come back in on the other side of the arena.
GLOVE.DESC: An orange glass tile with a big glove holding a bomb up.
GLOVE.NOTE_1: Drop, pick up, throw: all on the bomb key. No new button to learn, and the rules decide from where you stand and what you hold.
GLOVE.NOTE_2: A thrown bomb or player flies over crates, stone and bombs. Where it cannot land it bounces one tile on; past the edge of the arena it comes back in on the other side.
GLOVE.NOTE_3: The fuse never stops while you carry it, and a flame where you stand sets it off. The bomb is always yours: a kill with it counts for you.

KICK.NAME: Kick
KICK.EFFECT: Walk into a bomb, anyone’s, and it hops one tile on. With a crate, stone or another bomb in the way, it jumps over to the next free tile.
KICK.DESC: A purple glass tile with a sneaker kicking a bomb.
KICK.NOTE_1: You only walk. Bumping into a bomb from the middle of a tile is the kick; kick again to send it further.
KICK.NOTE_2: Each kick moves the bomb a single tile, jumping whatever is in the way and wrapping round the arena edge, like the glove.
KICK.NOTE_3: Kicking does not make a bomb yours: whoever dropped it gets the kill. Its fuse keeps burning in the air.

ITEMS.KEY_GLOVE: Bomb key: drop, pick up, throw
ITEMS.KEY_GLOVE_HINT: Press it on the bomb you just dropped to pick it up, and again to throw it the way you face.

WALLPASS.NAME: Wall pass
WALLPASS.EFFECT: Walk through crates as if they were not there. Stone and walls are still walls.
WALLPASS.DESC: A brick-coloured glass with a figure stepping out of a wall.
WALLPASS.NOTE_1: Inside a crate the fire cannot reach you: the flame stops at the brick. But once the crate blows up, the next flame gets you.
WALLPASS.NOTE_2: Hidden in the campaign stages. It comes to versus once the bots learn to use it.
WALLPASS.NOTE_3: Like the other items, it carries over to the next stage — until you lose.

FULLFIRE.NAME: Full fire
FULLFIRE.EFFECT: Takes your fire straight to the limit, 8 cells.
FULLFIRE.DESC: An orange glass with a big flame over a full gauge.
FULLFIRE.NOTE_1: Worth every fire item at once. Rare on purpose.
FULLFIRE.NOTE_2: Full reach crosses the arena: plan the way out before you drop.

POWERBOMB.NAME: Power bomb
POWERBOMB.EFFECT: The first bomb of each volley reaches as far as fire goes; the rest use your normal fire.
POWERBOMB.DESC: A red glass with a big bomb glowing inside.
POWERBOMB.NOTE_1: Only a bomb dropped with none of yours on the ground is a power bomb. Drop, wait for it to go off, and the next one is a power bomb again.
POWERBOMB.NOTE_2: The bots plan their escape with the power bomb’s reach.
POWERBOMB.NOTE_3: It carries over to the next stage with the rest of your kit.

SKULL.NAME: Skull
SKULL.EFFECT: A curse for 10 seconds: dropping bombs non-stop, not being able to drop any, reversed controls, slow, too fast, or a short fuse. Touching another player passes it on.
SKULL.DESC: A dark glass with a pale skull.
SKULL.NOTE_1: The only item that hurts whoever picks it up. It lies on the floor like the others: look before you step on it.
SKULL.NOTE_2: Touch, and it moves on: whoever had it is free. It does not come straight back — it takes a second before it can pass again.
SKULL.NOTE_3: Drawn from the moment and the cell, the same on every screen. The skull floats over your head while it lasts.

CLOCK.NAME: Clock
CLOCK.EFFECT: Puts 30 seconds back on the clock — while the walls have not started closing.
CLOCK.DESC: A blue glass with a clock face.
CLOCK.NOTE_1: Handy in the busiest stages, when time runs short.
CLOCK.NOTE_2: Once the walls start dropping, the clock does not turn back.
CLOCK.NOTE_3: In versus, the round’s clock is the same for everyone.

ONEUP.NAME: Extra life
ONEUP.EFFECT: One more life in the campaign.
ONEUP.DESC: A pink glass with a heart.
ONEUP.NOTE_1: Found in few stages and in the bonus stage.
ONEUP.NOTE_2_TITLE: It counts even if you fall
ONEUP.NOTE_2: Picked up, it is yours: the life counts even if you lose the stage afterwards.
ONEUP.NOTE_3: There are no lives to win in versus.

SOUNDS.TITLE: Sounds
SOUNDS.LEAD: Everything the game plays, to hear on its own: the arena theme, each effect and every line of the announcer. All of it is synthesised in the browser — no recordings, nothing to license.
SOUNDS.HOW_DESC: Music and effects are Web Audio oscillators and noise; the announcer is the browser’s own Portuguese voice, so it sounds a little different on each device.
SOUNDS.EFFECTS_LEAD: One button per effect, as the game plays it.
SOUNDS.QUIPS_LEAD: Original lines in Brazilian Portuguese, one moment at a time. In a match only a few crates get a comment, and never two lines within 2.5 s.
SOUNDS.NOTE_1: Bouncy and major like the arena games of the 16-bit era, but the tune is ours, note by note. The score lives in `score.ts` as readable text.
SOUNDS.NOTE_2: No quotes from any show and no imitation of anyone: the lines are ours, in the spirit of a loud neighbour at the window.
SOUNDS.NOTE_3: Every sound goes through one class each (music, effects, voice), so recorded music or voice lines can replace the synthesis without touching the game.
SOUNDS.ITEMS_HINT: Each item’s pick-up sound and its announcer lines live on the item’s own page.
SOUNDS.VOICE_HINT: Only this browser’s Portuguese voices; the choice is remembered here and used in matches.
SOUNDS.VOICE_NONE: This browser has no Portuguese voice; the announcer stays quiet.

ONLINE.TITLE: Online
ONLINE.LEAD: One public arena for up to {{max}} players. Watch the round, join the queue, and the next round starts as soon as {{min}} are in line. While a round is on, the first in line stand outside the wall throwing bombs in — a kill puts you in.
ONLINE.CONTROLS: Move with WASD or the arrow keys · Space or Enter drops a bomb (or throws one from outside) · Shift or Ctrl uses the mount · E or / sets off your bombs once you have the remote control.

RULES.TITLE: Room rules
RULES.LEAD: How this room plays. The leader can change these; a change made during a round applies to the next one.
RULES.ADMIN_HINT: You lead this room. A change applies at once between rounds, or to the next round while one is on.
RULES.PENDING: Change scheduled for the next round
RULES.OUTSIDERS_DESC: How many of the queue stand on the wall throwing bombs in. 0 turns it off.
RULES.FALLEN_OUTSIDE: Fallen fight back from the wall
RULES.FALLEN_OUTSIDE_DESC: Whoever falls goes to the wall (when the line leaves room) and is back in the arena on a kill. Off, the fallen just watch.
RULES.MIN_PLAYERS_DESC: The countdown starts with this many in line.
RULES.MAX_PLAYERS_DESC: A full arena starts at once — with the arena vote, as soon as everyone is ready.
RULES.COUNTDOWN_MS_DESC: How long the room waits for more players.
RULES.MAP_VOTE_DESC: During the countdown the next round’s players pick the arena — picking means ready — and the round starts once everyone is. The most voted wins; a tie or no votes, a draw. Off: the arena is drawn.
RULES.RESULTS_MS_DESC: How long the winner stays up before the next round.
RULES.ROUND_TIMER_MS_DESC: How long a round lasts. Off means no clock.
RULES.CLOSING_WALLS_DESC: When the clock runs out, walls fall in a spiral until one is left. Off: time-up is a draw.
RULES.DROP_ITEMS_DESC: Whoever falls leaves what they picked up scattered across the arena for the others. Off: the items fall with them.
RULES.WINNER_STAYS_DESC: The winner plays the next round with the next in line, up to this many wins in a row; then to the back of the line. Off: every player goes to the back.
RULES.BOTS_DESC: How many bots play by themselves while someone watches and nobody is in line. 0: no bots.
RULES.BOTS_FILL_TO_DESC: With people in line, bots complete the round up to this many players: with 3, one person plays two bots, two play one, three or more play without bots. Off: bots never play with people.
RULES.BOT_LEVEL_DESC: How well the bots play. Medium is the room's usual; hard bots read chains, set traps and never hesitate.
RULES.IDLE_MS_DESC: A player who sends nothing for this long is taken out of the round and the line. Off: nobody is ever removed for standing still.

CAMPAIGN.TITLE: Stages
CAMPAIGN.LEAD: Critters have taken over the city. Cross each area with up to 3 friends, stage by stage, up to the boss. Beating the boss opens the next area.

AREA_HINT.locked: Beat the previous area’s boss to open it.

CAMPAIGN.MAP_SOON: This area’s map is still being drawn.

HOW.TITLE: How it works
HOW.STEP_1: Join alone or with up to 3 friends, each with the character they picked.
HOW.STEP_2: Take down every critter with bombs.
HOW.STEP_3: Find the gate hidden under a block — it opens when the last critter falls.
HOW.STEP_4: 3 lives per area: losing one costs what you gathered. The 1-Up gives one more.

KIT.TITLE: Your strength
KIT.LEAD: What you pick up in a stage comes with you to the next, up to the limit. Died? You lose a life and what you gathered.

SIGNIN.LEAD: Sign in to play the stages.
SIGNIN.FAILED: Could not sign in right now. Try again.
SIGNIN.VERIFY: Confirm your e-mail to play: open the link we sent you.

COLLECTION.TITLE: Collection
COLLECTION.LEAD: Every boss and critter of the campaign. The ones you have not reached yet stay in the dark.

HINT.locked: Open this area to meet its boss.
HINT.soon: This area arrives in a future update.

GRAMADO_1.NAME: Park Gate
GRAMADO_1.DESC: The stage to learn on: only leafcutter ants, slow and easy. Take down all 6 and find the gate.

GRAMADO_2.NAME: Bandstand
GRAMADO_2.DESC: The pigeons arrive: fast and aimless, they take off when a bomb lands nearby.

GRAMADO_3.NAME: Promenade
GRAMADO_3.DESC: Snails survive two blasts and leave a slime trail that slows you down.

GRAMADO_4.NAME: The Nest
GRAMADO_4.DESC: Lapwings dash at anyone in their row. Every critter at once.

GRAMADO_5.NAME: Royal Anthill
GRAMADO_5.DESC: The mother of the leafcutters digs under the arena and cracks the ground to come out. Beat her to open the Substation.

SUBESTACAO_1.NAME: Gatehouse
SUBESTACAO_1.DESC: Two screens to learn the moving screen: clear the critters on the first, find the key the possum carries on the second.

SUBESTACAO_2.NAME: Arc Lines
SUBESTACAO_2.DESC: Here come the wasps, flying over the crates. Two screens to cross without getting cornered.

SUBESTACAO_3.NAME: Generator Room
SUBESTACAO_3.DESC: The sparks keep coming and the short bursts when it falls: make its blast work for you.

SUBESTACAO_4.NAME: The Escape
SUBESTACAO_4.DESC: Three screens with everything the Substation has. At the end the floor gives way and drops you into the cellar.

SUBESTACAO_5.NAME: Cable Cellar
SUBESTACAO_5.DESC: The Wire Cat waits in the dark. Use the crates as a shield from its zap and strike when it goes dark.

GRAMADO_BONUS.NAME: Lake Bonus
GRAMADO_BONUS.DESC: No critters, an item under every block and 30 seconds to grab what you can. There is even an extra life hidden.

SAUVA.NAME: Leafcutter
SAUVA.DESC: Slow and absent-minded, carrying her leaf. Walks straight and turns any way when she bumps into something.

POMBO.NAME: Pigeon
POMBO.DESC: Fast and aimless: picks a new way at every crossing. Flies off when a bomb is placed nearby.

CARAMUJO.NAME: Snail
CARAMUJO.DESC: Very slow, but the shell survives one blast. Leaves a slime trail that slows whoever steps on it.

QUEROQUERO.NAME: Lapwing
QUEROQUERO.DESC: Patrols slowly and dashes at anyone in the same row or column, until it hits something.

FAISCA.NAME: Spark
FAISCA.DESC: Fast and aimless: it takes a new way at every crossing. The generators churn them out.

GAMBA.NAME: Possum
GAMBA.DESC: The first blast flips it on its back for 3 s, harmless. Then it is up and running faster.

MARIMBONDO.NAME: Wasp
MARIMBONDO.KIND: From the nest on the pole
MARIMBONDO.DESC: Flies over the crates towards the nearest player. Crates are no cover: only fire gets it.

CURTO.NAME: Short
CURTO.DESC: Walks straight on and, when it falls, bursts in a cross: crates, other critters and anyone beside it.

RAINHA.NAME: Leafcutter Queen
RAINHA.DESC: The mother of every leafcutter in the park. Digs under the arena, cracks the ground to come out and is dizzy for 2 s — the time to strike.

GATO.NAME: Wire Cat
GATO.DESC: The cellar’s tangle of wires come to life. It stops, glows and zaps its row and column — crates block it; after every zap it is drained for 2 s: the time to strike.
